subject: Telemetry digest & recommended model lanes — Remedi Health pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@remedihealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry digest & recommended model lanes — Remedi Health pilot

Hi Alex / Sara —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick post-call digest with the telemetry highlights and the concrete model lanes we'd recommend for the pilot. I kept the asks and next steps at the bottom.

Summary (high level)
- Primary workload: long-form clinical note summarization + structured extraction.
- Constraint: 95th percentile response time target <= 250ms for short summaries; longer jobs can be async.
- Quality constraint: low hallucination tolerance for diagnoses and medication entities; want regression guardrails.

Redwood-verified model lanes (recommended)
1) rw-instruct-13b-q4f16 (recommended primary)
   - Typical single-GPU throughput (small batch): ~45 TPS
   - Latency percentiles (measured on G5-like instance, 512-token sequences): p50 72ms, p95 210ms, p99 430ms
   - Notes: strongest extractive accuracy on our clinical prompt set; slightly higher cost but fewer prompt-engineering workarounds.

2) rw-chat-7b-8bit (cost-optimized fallback)
   - Typical throughput: ~90 TPS
   - Latency: p50 38ms, p95 120ms, p99 240ms
   - Notes: good for short summaries and light-weight routing; observed ~3% higher entity hallucination in our verification prompts — recommend post-hoc entity filter for PII/medication fields.

3) rw-compact-4b (experimental)
   - Use-case: high-concurrency daytime spikes where latency SLOs matter more than absolute extractive recall.
   - Throughput: >180 TPS, p95 ~95ms.

Artifacts shared
- Redwood perf profiles (live): https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/rw-instruct-13b-q4f16
- Telemetry snapshot we captured during today's demo: drive link (CSV) and quick traces — attached: telemetry_snapshot_20260517.csv
- Prompt bundle used for verification (zipped): remedi_prompt_bundle_v1.zip

Quality / regression notes
- We saw one failure mode on long context (>= 2k tokens) with rw-chat-7b-8bit where medication lists were truncated; rw-instruct-13b-q4f16 handled these more robustly.
- Recommendation: include the provided prompt regression harness as a pre-deploy check and wire it to Redwood Optimize alerts (we can enable a webhook to your SRE).

Next steps / asks
- Please confirm acceptance of the two-lane pilot (13B primary, 7B fallback) and whether you want us to include the 4B experimental lane for daytime bursts.
- I'll upload a shortcanary rollout config for your infra team; Marcus can work with your SRE to set capacity targets.
- Action: schedule a 30-min ops sync this week with your infra lead.

Thanks — attaching the prompt bundle and telemetry snapshot.

—
Jordan Blake

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@remedihealth.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@remedihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry digest & recommended model lanes — Remedi Health pilot

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions:  

1) SLA / fallback behavior: if daytime spikes cause the 13B lane to breach p95 > 250ms, what's the recommended automated fallback? Do you push to 7B or the 4B lane? How do you avoid quality regressions when that happens?

2) Regression monitoring: can Redwood run the prompt regression harness on every deploy and surface the top 10 failing prompts to our SRE/Clinical QA? What alert channels would that use?

3) Data residency: small ask — can the telemetry CSVs and perf traces be stored in our AWS account S3 (we prefer to keep logs in our account)?

FWIW Sara and I liked the 13B results on the medication extraction tests. We'd prefer to start pilot with 13B primary + 7B fallback, but we want the fallback to be conservative for entity-sensitive responses (i.e., route entity extraction to 13B when confidence is below a threshold).

On scheduling — I'm available Wednesday/Thursday mornings PT.

—Alex
Alex Reed
Head of ML Engineering, Remedi Health
alex.reed@remedihealth.com

Hi Alex — quick answers inline:  

1) Fallback behavior: our recommended default is an automated model routing policy that tries rw-instruct-13b first and falls back to rw-chat-7b for latency-sensitive requests. For entity-sensitive workflows we can add a cheap classifier (confidence threshold) that keeps extraction routed to 13B when confidence < 0.85.

2) Regression monitoring: yes — we can run the regression harness on every model rollout and push failures to your team's Slack channel + create GitHub issues in a shared repo. We can also expose the top-10 failing prompts as a daily report to an S3 bucket you control.

3) Data residency: we support pushing telemetry artifacts to a customer-owned S3 bucket; Marcus will send the sample bucket policy.

I'll propose Wed 10:00 PT for an ops sync — Jordan / Marcus, can you confirm?

—Vanessa

Alex / team — following up with capacity numbers and the sample bucket policy.

Capacity (recommendation for initial 3-week pilot)
- 13B lane: 2 reserved GPUs (sustains ~80-90 concurrent short requests, headroom to 120 TPS with burst)
- 7B lane: 1 reserved GPU (handles fallback traffic, scales to ~180 TPS with autoscale)
- Autoscaling: recommend adding a 1-GPU burst pool for daytime spikes.

I've attached a short capacity worksheet (capacity_worksheet_may2026.xlsx) with the projected cost delta for the three-week pilot vs expected savings from batching/caching.

Bucket policy / telemetry: sample policy link: https://drive.redwood.ai/configs/remedi-s3-bucket-policy.txt — we'll share a CloudFormation snippet in the ops call.

Next steps (concrete)
- Jordan: upload the canary rollout config to HubSpot / your infra repo.
- Alex / Remedi: confirm S3 bucket + preferred Slack channel for alerts.
- Schedule: Ops sync Wed 10:00 PT (tentatively) — invite sent.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.
